claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout monitoring/rollback controls make launch acceptable, provided the known enterprise refund workflow limitation is disclosed at launch.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if admissible evidence shows the internal policy threshold for launch is satisfied.
If the affected use case remains exposed, rollout controls and monitoring cannot substitute for required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Operational readiness evidence can support launch posture, but it does not cure a model-card disclosure deficiency by itself.
Independent support requires direct evidence of the relevant policy text, the actual exposure status of the affected segment, and the completed disclosure or approved exception.
evidence_requests: The actual internal release or certification standard showing whether launch may proceed with an unresolved disclosed limitation.
The launch model-card or equivalent disclosure artifact confirming the enterprise refund workflow limitation is explicitly documented before launch.
The underlying evaluation record for the enterprise refund workflow gap, including threshold, measured performance, and why the gap is considered material or non-material.
Any approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment.
The source documents behind each cited evidence ID, not just the actor summary.
specific_concerns: The available record is only the actor's summary, so the cited evidence cannot be independently checked for scope, wording, or thresholds.

The policy text says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed, and the actor admits that the enterprise refund workflow remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The actor's packet appears to rely on a future disclosure step, but no admissible evidence in this role confirms that the launch materials will in fact contain the required limitation disclosure.
There is no approved risk acceptance on the present record, and the actor concedes the existing draft does not cover the exposed enterprise refund workflow.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not by themselves resolve the model-card disclosure predicate for the exposed use case.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record rather than merely arguable if launch disclosure is actually completed.
That the cited public guidance is sufficient to bridge the unresolved internal policy predicate for the exposed enterprise refund workflow.
That monitoring, rollback, and a 4% rollout materially support certification beyond operational safeguards, given the policy expressly says such controls do not remove disclosure duties.
